'''Orlando Auciello''' is an Argentine-born materials scientist and physicist. He is a Distinguished Endowed Chair Professor in the Departments of Materials Science and Engineering and Bioengineering at the [[University of Texas at Dallas]] (2013–present).<ref name="UTDprofile">{{cite web |url=https://profiles.utdallas.edu/orlando.auciello |title=Orlando Auciello - UT Dallas Profiles |publisher=The University of Texas at Dallas |access-date=2026-02-20}}</ref><ref name="BEUTD">{{cite web |url=https://be.utdallas.edu/people/faculty/orlando-auciello |title=Orlando Auciello |publisher=Bioengineering - The University of Texas at Dallas |access-date=2026-02-20}}</ref>

He previously served as a Distinguished Fellow and senior scientist at [[Argonne National Laboratory]] (1996-2012), where he co-developed ultrananocrystalline diamond (UNCD) thin-film technology.<ref name="asn2013">{{cite web |url=https://www.advancedsciencenews.com/startups-in-materials-science-interview-with-orlando-auciello-2 |title=Startups in materials science: interview with Orlando Auciello |publisher=Advanced Science News |date=2013-03-04 |access-date=2026-02-20}}</ref><ref name="anl2019">{{cite web |url=https://www.anl.gov/article/john-crane-acquires-division-of-advanced-diamond-technologies-a-company-built-on-argonne-technology |title=John Crane acquires division of Advanced Diamond Technologies, a company built on Argonne technology |publisher=Argonne National Laboratory |author=Alex Mitchell |date=2019-06-19 |access-date=2026-02-20}}</ref> Auciello co-founded Advanced Diamond Technologies in 2003 to commercialize UNCD-based products, including mechanical pump seals, bearings, and AFM tips with significantly enhanced performance; the company's industrial division was acquired by John Crane in 2019.<ref name="anl2019" /><ref name="asn2013" />

He also co-founded Original Biomedical Implants (OBI-USA, 2013–present; OBI-México, 2016-present), focused on developing and commercializing next-generation medical implants and prostheses coated with biocompatible UNCD for applications such as dental implants, orthopedic devices, and biosensors.<ref name="scientia2022">{{cite web |url=https://www.scientia.global/dr-orlando-auciello-ultrananocrystalline-diamond-coatings-for-transformational-medical-devices-and-prostheses |title=Dr Orlando Auciello - Ultrananocrystalline Diamond (UNCD) Medical Devices and Prostheses |publisher=Scientia |date=2022-11-09 |access-date=2026-02-20}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Auciello was born in Córdoba, Argentina.<ref name="scientia2022"/> He completed a program in electronic engineering at the [[National University of Córdoba]] from 1964 to 1970.<ref name="scientia2022"/> He received his MS in physics in 1973 and PhD in physics in 1976 from the Physics Institute "Dr. Balseiro" at the Universidad Nacional de Cuyo-Argentina.<ref name="scientia2022"/>

== Career ==
Auciello conducted research as postdoc at [[McMaster University]] (1977-1979) and Senior Scientists the [[University of Toronto]] (1979-1984).<ref name="scientia2022"/> He was an associate professor at [[North Carolina State University]] (1985-1988) and a senior scientist at the Microelectronics Center of North Carolina (1988-1996).<ref name="scientia2022"/> At [[Argonne National Laboratory]] (1996-2012), becoming a Distinguished Fellow in 2010.<ref name="scientia2022"/>

In 2012, Auciello became a Distinguished Endowed Chair Professor at the [[University of Texas at Dallas]].<ref name="scientia2022"/> He has held adjunct professorships at the [[University of Colorado Colorado Springs]] and [[Michigan State University]].<ref name="scientia2022"/> Auciello retired from UTD in December 31, 2025

Auciello was president of the [[Materials Research Society]] in 2013.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mrs-bulletin/article/auciello-leads-mrs-board-of-directors-for-2013/3B21E88B11BBE9A854E01969AEFECF6D|title=Auciello leads MRS Board of Directors for 2013|journal=MRS Bulletin| publisher=Cambridge University Press|access-date=2026-02-12}}</ref>

== Research ==
Auciello R&D focuses on  multifunctional oxide thin films for [[ferroelectric random-access memory]] (FeRAM), high-dielectric constant films for super-capacitors, and  piezoelectric films for new generation of sensors.<ref name="scientia2022"/> He co-developed UNCD films for applications in [[Microelectromechanical systems|MEMS]] / [[Nanoelectromechanical systems|NEMS]], electron emitters, and biomedical devices.<ref name="asn2013"/><ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/ultrananocrystalline-diamond%20(UNCD)-coatings%20-for-nextgeneration-hightech-and-medical-devices/020C73B85EAD75C9E386A7006D8E1C19|title=Ultrananocrystalline Diamond Coatings for Next-Generation High-Tech and Medical Devices|publisher=Cambridge University Press|date=July 8, 2022|access-date=2026-02-12}}</ref>

UNCD coating technology contributed to the coating of the [[Argus II]] retinal prosthesis, which returned partial vision to people blind by retinas pigmentosa.<ref name="kera2014">{{cite web|url=https://www.keranews.org/health-science-tech/2014-01-08/lab-grown-diamonds-could-give-medical-implants-new-shine|title=Lab-Grown Diamonds Could Give Medical Implants New Shine |publisher=KERA News|date=January 8, 2014|access-date=2026-02-12}}</ref>

As of 2026, Auciello has an h-index of 79 and over 28,000 citations.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=5BZcLWQAAAAJ|title=Orlando Auciello|publisher=Google Scholar|access-date=2026-02-12}}</ref> He holds 20 patents.<ref name="tandfonline.com">{{cite journal|url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/26941112.2022.2033606|title=Science and technology of a transformational multifunctional ultrananocrystalline diamond (UNCD TM ) coating|journal=Functional Diamond|volume=2|issue=1|pages=1–18|date=2022|doi=10.1080/26941112.2022.2033606|access-date=2026-02-12|doi-access=free}}</ref>

=== Oxide thin films ===
Auciello has worked on oxide thin films for applications in ferroelectric random-access memories (FeRAMs], high-dielectric constant devices, and supercapacitors.<ref name="scientia2022"/>

=== Ultrananocrystalline diamond ===
Auciello co-invented (with Gruen and Krauss) the UNCD film technology with grain sizes of 2-5&nbsp;nm.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S092596351000141X|title=Status review of the science and technology of ultrananocrystalline diamond (UNCD™) films and application to multifunctional devices|journal=Diamond and Related Materials|volume=19|issue=7-9|pages=621–640|date=2010|doi=10.1016/j.diamond.2010.03.015|access-date=2026-02-12|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Applications include RF MEMS/NEMS, field emission cathodes, and coatings for mechanical seals, bearings, AFM tips and biomedical implants.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.openaccessgovernment.org/article/ultrananocrystalline-diamond-coating-uncd-revolutionizing-surface-engineering/174035|title=Ultrananocrystalline diamond coating (UNCD™): Revolutionizing surface engineering|publisher=Open Access Government|date=February 28, 2024|access-date=2026-02-12}}</ref>

== Entrepreneurship ==
Auciello co-founded (with J.A. Carlisle and N. Kane) Advanced Diamond Technologies (ADT) in 2003 to commercialize the UNCD coating technology. The company was acquired by [[John Crane Inc.]] in 2019.,<ref name="anl2019"/> which continues to commercialize the UNCD-coated industrial products.

Auciello founded Original Biomedical Implants, LLC (OBI-USA) in 2013, and co-founded (with Dr. J.L. Rubio-MD) OBI-México in 2016, to develop and market UNCD-coated medical devices and prostheses.<ref name="scientia2022"/>

== Awards and honors ==
* Fellow, [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (2009)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.anl.gov/article/argonne-scientist-orlando-auciello-named-aaas-fellow-for-contributions-in-materials-science|title=Argonne scientist Orlando Auciello named AAAS fellow for contributions in materials science|publisher=Argonne National Laboratory|date=January 5, 2009|access-date=2026-02-12}}</ref>
* Fellow, [[Materials Research Society]] (2009)<ref name="tandfonline.com"/>
* Seven R&D 100 Awards (including 2003 for large area ultrananocrystalline diamond technology, 2008 for commercialization of ultrananocrystalline diamond-coated mechanical pump seals, 2009 for artificial retina, 2011)<ref name="kera2014"/>
* Fellow, International Association of Advanced Materials (IAAM) (2023)<ref name="UTD2023Apr">{{cite web |url=https://news.utdallas.edu/campus-community/accolades-april-2023/ |title=Professor To Receive Scientist Medal; Students Win Brain Bowl |publisher=UT Dallas News |date=April 26, 2023 |access-date=February 20, 2026}}</ref>
